title: Standardize retry/timeout/backoff behavior and idempotency across services & SDKs
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Problem statement: disparate retry/timeout/backoff implementations across microservices and language SDKs are causing unpredictable tail latency and duplicate side-effects during multi-region failovers. We need a cross-team standard that: 1) defines default retry counts, backoff strategies, and timeouts tuned for our SLO targets; 2) mandates idempotency key semantics for mutating endpoints; 3) provides opt-in hedged request support for latency-sensitive routes; and 4) integrates with circuit breakers and load-shedding policies for overload protection. Scope: core HTTP/gRPC services, Redwood SDKs (JS, Python, Go), and gateway/proxy layer. Out of scope: third-party integrations and legacy internal admin tooling (handled in follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: A clear defaults doc published with numeric defaults for: initial timeout, per-attempt timeout, max attempts, jittered exponential backoff parameters, and total operation deadline
SDKs (JS/Python/Go) updated with identical retry policy primitives and a single configuration source (env var + runtime override), passing language-specific test suites
Idempotency header defined (X-Redwood-Idempotency) with generation/spec guidance and server-side validation returning 409 for conflicting idempotency tokens
Hedged request mechanism implemented at gateway for configured routes with feature flag and telemetry that shows p50/p99 impact
Circuit-breaker integration documented and enabled for routes with high CPU or GPU pressure with observable trip events in Console
Migration plan executed for top 20 customer-facing endpoints with staged rollout and rollback criteria
test_plan: Unit tests for SDK retry/backoff logic with deterministic clock
Chaos experiments: region failover + synthetic traffic to validate no duplicate writes when idempotency headers present
Load tests showing latency and throughput with hedging enabled vs disabled
Integration tests for server-side idempotency store and edge-case conflict behavior
E2E smoke against a canary release using runtime-2.6
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Gateway hedging and SDK opt-in flags enabled for internal services only (1 week)
Phase 2 (limited customer): SDK defaults turned on for beta customers and observability dashboards monitored (2 weeks)
Phase 3 (wider rollout): Gradually enable defaults for all services with per-route overrides and a week-long monitoring window
Rollback: global env toggle at the gateway and per-service feature flags; immediate rollback if p99 increases > 2x or error rate increases above SLA threshold

notes_and_open_questions: How aggressive should hedged requests be for GPU-backed model endpoints where duplicate in-flight requests have monetary cost? (action: cost estimator from infra)
Should we prefer idempotency keys for all POST/PUTs or only for endpoints that mutate persistent state? (decision leaning: require for all externally-facing mutating endpoints)
What is the canonical header name and expected token entropy? (proposal: X-Redwood-Idempotency, 128-bit RFC4122 UUID + optional client-supplied context)
Telemetry: define metrics to track - attempted_retries, successful_retries, idempotency_conflicts, hedged_savings_ms
Backward compatibility: SDKs must default to previous behaviour for one minor release and expose opt-in env var; migration docs needed
